1.why: All MFA endpoints gate on owner(), which requires an authenticated session whose userId equals ACCOUNT.id, so settings are only reachable for the signed-in account owner.

2.why: Identity OTPs are bound to the pre-auth session that issued them and TOTP/backup checks use the account’s own secret/hashes, so the same code does not authenticate as another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/confirm only writes mfaRecords and does not invalidate or rotate any other existing authenticated sessions.

4.why: OTP secrets are stored with AES-GCM (encryptedSecret) and backup codes are stored only as HMAC digests in backupHashes.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, OTP seeds, and backup codes are produced with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session cookie is __Host- with HttpOnly; client code keeps secrets only in in-memory JS variables, not localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validBackup) reject malformed input before auth/MFA logic runs.

8.why: User- and API-derived values are applied via textContent (and JSON APIs), not unescaped HTML insertion, blocking markup/script execution.

9.why: The app performs no HTTP redirects at all, so open redirects are absent even though no explicit redirect allow-list is implemented.

10.why: headers() sets CSP (with frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on the __Host-mfa_session cookie.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces and tokens stay out of URLs, but demo API fields and the client log panel deliberately surface OTPs and backup codes.

13.why: Identity codes expire via identityExpiresAt and are consumed with the session; TOTP counters are recorded as used; backup codes are removed from the hash set after success.

14.why: Identity, authenticator, and recovery paths use attempt counters with lockout after MAX_FAILURES for LOCK_MS (429 when locked).

15.why: Successful /api/auth/verify deletes the pre-auth session and issues a new id; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
